edges.description: Reduced PHGDH activity lowers de novo L-serine synthesis, producing low L-serine and, secondarily, low glycine (derived from serine via serine hydroxymethyltransferase).
L-serine deficiency starves serine-dependent biosynthetic pathways in the developing brain — phospholipids, nucleotides, sphingolipids/myelin, and the neurotransmitters glycine and D-serine.
The biosynthetic deficit manifests as hypomyelination, congenital microcephaly, intractable seizures, and severe psychomotor retardation.
Decreased L-serine in plasma/CSF reports the PHGDH synthetic block and is the key diagnostic marker of serine-deficiency disorders.

evidence.snippet: Low concentrations of the amino acids serine, glycine as well as 5-methyltetrahydrofolate were found in plasma and CSF

readouts.interpretation: Decreased L-serine in plasma/CSF reports the PHGDH synthetic block and is the key diagnostic marker of serine-deficiency disorders.

nodes.description: Deprivation of serine-derived building blocks impairs myelin membrane synthesis (hypomyelination) and normal neurodevelopment, and disturbs glycine/D-serine-mediated neurotransmission, contributing to seizures. These downstream deficits explain why the phenotype is dominated by CNS disease.

evidence.snippet: an important role for PHGDH activity and L-serine biosynthesis in the metabolism, development, and function of the central nervous system

nodes.description: Oral L-serine supplementation, sometimes combined with glycine, replenishes the deficient amino acids. It reduces seizure frequency and, when begun early, can improve myelination and developmental outcome; addition of glycine can abolish seizures in patients incompletely controlled on L-serine alone. Serine-deficiency disorders are, unusually among neurometabolic disorders, potentially treatable.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that 3-PGDH can be treated effectively by a combination of L-serine and glycine.
can be treated with supplementation of L-serine, sometimes combined with glycine
A major reduction in seizure frequency occurred in all patients; two patients became free of seizures.
Early treatment with L-serine supplementation; glycine supplementation with L-serine has been used in some individuals

nodes.description: The block in de novo synthesis lowers L-serine, D-serine, and glycine in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid; reduced 5-methyltetrahydrofolate is also seen, reflecting serine's role as a one-carbon donor. The CNS is preferentially affected because serine crosses the blood-brain barrier poorly and depends on local synthesis.

biological_processes: serine family amino acid biosynthetic process

evidence.snippet: The biochemical abnormalities associated with this disorder are low concentrations of L-serine, D-serine, and glycine in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Low concentrations of the amino acids serine, glycine as well as 5-methyltetrahydrofolate were found in plasma and CSF

nodes.description: Convergent CNS phenotype of 3-PGDH deficiency: congenital microcephaly, intractable seizures, severe psychomotor retardation, and hypomyelination. Because the underlying deficiency is of a synthesizable amino acid, these manifestations are partly responsive to L-serine (± glycine) supplementation, especially when treatment starts early.

evidence.snippet: characterized by congenital microcephaly, psychomotor retardation, and seizures
Only two missense mutations (p.V425M and p.V490M) have been identified in PHGDH, the gene encoding 3-PGDH
predicted to change valine at position 490 to methionine
Homozygous mutations in PHGDH, a gene involved in the first and limiting step in L-serine biosynthesis, were recently identified as the cause of the disease

nodes.description: Biallelic PHGDH variants reduce or abolish 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase activity, the first and rate-limiting enzyme of the phosphorylated pathway of de novo L-serine biosynthesis (NAD+-dependent oxidation of 3-phosphoglycerate to 3-phosphohydroxypyruvate).
